about.title: Pleasanton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pleasanton sits where I-580 and I-680 meet, and that interchange shapes how collisions happen here. In 2025, the city recorded 324 injury collisions, with 447 people hurt and 3 lives lost. Public records show the heaviest collision counts along I-580 in both directions and on I-680 southbound, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when commuters head home through the Tri-Valley. If one of those crashes involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered. Medical visits pile up, the other driver's insurer starts calling, and your car may be sitting in a tow yard. LawProactive exists to take one task off your list. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Alameda County. That attorney works on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened once, and we handle the introduction.

items.title: The clock matters in California
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, the window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can pin down which deadline applies to your crash before it passes.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame for a collision on I-680 or a Pleasanton surface street, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your percentage. Insurers know this and may push to inflate your share.

items.title: Protect what you say and what you keep
items.desc: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so early can hurt you later. An attorney can handle those calls while you focus on preserving photos, repair estimates, and medical records.

items.question: My crash happened on I-580 in Pleasanton. Who investigates, and how do I get the report?
items.answer: Collisions on I-580 and I-680 are typically handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Pleasanton police, so the report request goes through CHP's Dublin-area office. It can take several days to a few weeks for the report to become available. An attorney can request it on your behalf and compare it against your own account and any dashcam or witness details.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are under no obligation to provide a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and it is generally wise not to. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault or minimize your injuries. Let an attorney communicate with them instead, and keep your own notes, photos, and medical paperwork organized in the meantime.

items.question: How much does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we do not charge you for the introduction. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery in your case, and the fee percentage is agreed on in writing before any work begins.
